Aerial Wildlife Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 503 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2021–2022) 
Background 
Wildlife Management Unit 503 ‘Lac La Biche’ (WMU 503) covers an area of 3,220 km² and is located in east-central Alberta, in 
the Boreal Central Mixedwood and Boreal Dry Mixedwood natural subregions. The WMU encompasses the hamlet and lake of 
Lac La Biche. The area of the lake of Lac La Biche (235.52km²) was removed from survey analyses for population estimates. 
Forests cover almost half of the landscape, including broadleaf forest (27%) coniferous forest (10%), and mixed-wood forest 
(7%). Agriculture covers 24% of the landscape. Sensitive wildlife areas include Great Blue Heron and American White Pelican 
colonial nesting sites, Sharp-tailed Grouse lek areas, Trumpeter Swan waterbodies, and 140 km² of key winter habitat for 
ungulates (‘Key Wildlife Biodiversity Zones’), and the northern part of the WMU is caribou range. 
The objective of the 2021/22 survey was to assess the status of ungulate populations (moose, white-tailed deer, and mule 
deer if adequate observations were obtained) in WMU 503 by estimating abundance, density and the age-sex composition. 
Survey method 
An aerial survey for ungulates was conducted January 18–21, 2022 using distance sampling techniques 
(Buckland et al., 2001, Thomas et al., 2010). A total of 106 north-south transect lines (survey effort = 869.37 km) were flown 
with one long ranger helicopter (Bell 206 LIII), equipped with rear bubble windows to maximize visibility. Ungulates were 
classified by age class (adult or juvenile) and sex. Other wildlife sightings were recorded, including 15 mule deer.  
Results 
Moose 
A total of 187 moose were observed in 129 groups and classified as 24 bulls (11 without antlers, 13 with one or both antlers), 
108 cows, 47 calves, and 8 unclassified. The estimated bull:cow:calf ratio was 22:100:44. The estimated density was 0.442 
moose/km² (90% CI 0.356–0.550; CV=0.132) and the estimated abundance was 1,320 moose (90% CI 1,062–1,641; 
CV=0.132), Results are summarized in Table 1. 
White-tailed deer 
A total of 776 white-tailed deer were observed in 267 groups and classified as 11 bucks (all with antlers), 59 does, 72 fawns, 
and 634 unclassified. The estimated buck:doe:fawn ratio was 19:100:122. Antler drop was assumed to be significant and the 
buck ratio is likely underestimated. The fawn ratio is likely overestimated, as a doe was typically only classified when a fawn 
was present. The estimated density was 2.165 white-tailed deer/km² (90% CI 1.785–2.626; CV=0.117) and estimated 
abundance was 6,462 white-tailed deer (90% CI 5,327–7,839; CV=0.117).
